$comment: Build inputs this repository chooses, in one place. Read by the workflow at
run time and passed to the Docker build as build arguments, so there is one
copy of each value and drift between consumers is not possible.
NOT here, deliberately:
* GitHub Action refs and the Dockerfile's FROM line. Those are literals in
their own files because a `uses:` reference cannot take an expression and
Dependabot needs a literal to rewrite. Copying them here would create a
second value to reconcile. See CLAUDE.md's merge procedure -- actions are
SHA-pinned and bumped by hand, measured 2026-08-12.
* nox-build/windows/vcpkg-ports.txt. It is the vcpkg download cache key, and
folding it in here would invalidate that cache whenever any unrelated pin
moved. No value participating in a cache key shares a file with values
that do not.
* Shape constants such as VCPKG_TRIPLET. They carry an invariant, not a
version, and separating a value from the comment explaining it is how the
invariant gets broken.
A tag is a movable ref. Where a tag is the thing fetched, the commit it
resolved to when reviewed is recorded beside it and asserted after the fetch,
so a moved tag fails the build instead of silently changing what ships.

qt.$comment: The version the Windows build has actually linked, read from QT_ROOT_DIR in a green run -- not the newest available. Pinning and upgrading are separate decisions.

$comment: Minimum acceptable values asserted against a running binary. These are not
the versions fetched -- they are the floor a build must clear, and they
move only when the reason for the floor changes.
libtorrent: SSL peer-cert matching is an exact comparison from 2.0.13.
Earlier versions compared only as many bytes as the certificate's own name,
so a leaf whose common name was a prefix of the torrent name authenticated
for it. Verify in torrent::verify_peer_cert, not from release notes --
upstream's changelog does not record the change.
webapi: the 5.1 to 5.2 boundary changed the API protocol.
